_README: TOPICAL TEMPLATE — Stage 2 scoped fact-build for 3 domains ABSENT from the standard facts-template.json (health/pharmacy/hospital billing, Balearic ferries, public holidays/closures). Same contract as the standard template: do NOT change field NAMES or STRUCTURE, fill VALUES only, keep every key (null if you can't fill it). Frame everything for the audience in _meta. STATUS MODEL: 'verified' = confirmed against an OFFICIAL source (URL in source_url); 'agreed_stable' = confident, no source opened; 'verify_recommended' = change-prone or high-stakes, flag it; 'serve_live' = volatile, must NOT be frozen (prices, exchange-driven costs). Return ONLY valid JSON in EXACTLY this structure. Fill EVERY section.
_fact_field_shape: Every FACT uses: { value, source_url, status (verified|agreed_stable|verify_recommended|serve_live), notes }. For 'verified' the source_url MUST be the official page you checked. Never invent a source.

health_care._note: Covers: Bringing Medication into Spain / Getting Treated in Barcelona: Pharmacy, Clinic or ER / What to Expect When a Spanish Hospital Bills You. YMYL — be conservative, prefer verify_recommended over agreed_stable.

prescription_medication_rules.value: Personal-use quantity for the duration of the trip (up to 90 days typically), in original packaging, with a doctor's letter or prescription in Spanish or English.
prescription_medication_rules.notes: quantity limits (e.g. ~personal supply for trip length), need for original packaging / doctor's letter or prescription copy

controlled_substances_note.value: Narcotics/psychotropics require a Schengen Certificate (or equivalent) issued by the traveler's home country; otherwise may be seized.
controlled_substances_note.notes: narcotics/psychotropics — Schengen certificate requirement for travelers carrying controlled meds across borders

farmacia_identification.value: Green cross sign (often lit or neon); may say 'Farmacia'.

farmacia_de_guardia.value: 24-hour rotating duty pharmacy; posted on all pharmacy doors or online at https://www.farmaciasdeguardia.com (or local city website).
farmacia_de_guardia.notes: 24h rotating duty-pharmacy system — how a tourist finds the open one

otc_vs_prescription_differences.value: Many antihistamines, ibuprofen (up to 600 mg), and some topical antifungals are OTC; antibiotics and codeine products are Rx-only.
otc_vs_prescription_differences.notes: things OTC in Spain but Rx-only in the US or vice versa

pharmacist_role.value: Pharmacists can diagnose and treat minor ailments (e.g., sore throat, mild infections, travel diarrhea) and may dispense certain stronger meds without a prescription under their discretion.
pharmacist_role.notes: Spanish pharmacists routinely advise/treat minor ailments directly

private_clinic_access.value: Walk-in private clinics (e.g., Creu Blanca, Quirónsalud) available; typical self-pay visit ~€80–€200 ($90–$220) plus tests.
private_clinic_access.notes: walk-in private clinics for tourists — typical cost range

public_hospital_er_access.value: Public ER ('urgencias') treats anyone regardless of residency; you may be asked for insurance/passport but cannot be denied emergency care. Non-residents may receive a bill later.
public_hospital_er_access.notes: urgencias access for non-residents, triage-based, whether insurance card is asked for AT the door

when_to_choose_which.value: RECOMMENDATION — For minor issues (e.g., fever, rash, cut) go to a pharmacy first or private clinic; for severe pain, difficulty breathing, chest pain, or major trauma call 112 or go directly to a public ER.
when_to_choose_which.notes: RECOMMENDATION — minor issue vs true emergency (112) decision guide

billing_model_public.value: Public hospitals generally bill non-EU tourists after treatment, often via mail to the patient's home address, or a bill can be requested at the hospital's administrative office. Payment may be required before discharge for non-emergency services.
billing_model_public.notes: does a public hospital bill a non-EU tourist directly, and when — at discharge or by mail

billing_model_private.value: Private clinics typically ask for credit card guarantee or upfront payment (partial or full) before treatment, especially for non-emergencies.

typical_costs.notes: rough ranges only: ER visit, ambulance ride, one overnight stay — never frozen as durable prices

travel_insurance_necessity.value: RECOMMENDATION — Strongly recommended; without it, a serious incident can cost tens of thousands of dollars. Many US health plans do not cover foreign treatment, and Medicare does not.
travel_insurance_necessity.notes: RECOMMENDATION — is it a hard requirement in practice for this audience

what_to_keep_for_reimbursement.value: Itemized invoice ('factura'), medical report ('informe médico'), and payment receipts; request them in Spanish (and ask for a translation or English version if possible).
what_to_keep_for_reimbursement.notes: itemized invoice / informe médico / payment receipts for a US insurer claim

ferries_balearics._note: Covers: Ferries from Barcelona to the Balearics: Fast vs Slow / When a Balearic Ferry Cancels, and What You're Owed.

operators.notes: e.g. Trasmediterránea, Baleària — who actually runs Barcelona-Balearics

port_terminal.value: Moll de Sant Bertran or Moll de Barcelona (Terminal Baleària and Trasmediterránea respectively). Accessible by Metro L2 (Drassanes) or bus 120.
port_terminal.notes: which Port de Barcelona terminal, how to get there from the center

to_palma_mallorca.value: Fast ferry ~2.5–3 hours; slow ferry ~6–8 hours (overnight or day). Rough price range: fast ~€80–150 ($90–170), slow ~€40–80 ($45–90) one-way, depending on season.
to_palma_mallorca.notes: fast vs slow ferry duration + rough price range

to_ibiza.value: Fast ferry ~4 hours; slow ferry ~8–10 hours. Rough price range: fast ~€100–180 ($110–200), slow ~€60–100 ($70–110).

to_menorca.value: Most ferries are via Mallorca (routing) or seasonal direct; direct slow ferry from Barcelona ~8–10 hours, fast ~4.5 hours. Rough price range: fast ~€100–160, slow ~€50–90; seasonal (summer only for some direct).
to_menorca.notes: note if it's direct or routed via Mallorca/Valencia, and seasonality

fast_vs_slow_tradeoffs.value: RECOMMENDATION — Choose fast if time-limited or prone to seasickness; choose slow if you want an overnight cabin to save a hotel night, or are bringing a car. Families may prefer the slower boat for more space and onboard amenities.
fast_vs_slow_tradeoffs.notes: RECOMMENDATION — price/time/overnight-cabin tradeoff, who should pick which

booking_advice.value: Book at least 2–3 weeks in advance for summer (July–August); walk-on tickets can sell out. Car spaces sell out weeks ahead. Buy directly from operator sites (Baleària or Trasmediterránea) to avoid third-party change fees.
booking_advice.notes: how far ahead in summer, walk-on vs car ferry, aggregator vs operator site

typical_causes.value: Wind speeds above ~40–50 knots, sea state (wave height) exceeding safety limits, port closures, or mechanical issues.

passenger_rights.value: Under EU Regulation 1177/2010, passengers have rights to re-routing, reimbursement, or assistance (meals, accommodation if overnight delay) depending on cancellation timing. Cash compensation only if cancellation is within operator's control; weather cancellations typically do not trigger cash compensation but do require re-routing or refund.
passenger_rights.notes: EU ferry passenger rights regulation — compensation, rerouting, care obligations

operator_rebooking_practice.value: Operators generally rebook on next available sailing (usually the next day) or offer a full refund; often can be done online or at the port ticket office.

travel_insurance_interaction.value: Standard travel insurance may cover missed connections (e.g., flight) or extra accommodation if the cancellation is due to weather or mechanical failure, but check your policy — many exclude 'acts of nature' unless you bought 'cancel for any reason' or severe weather coverage.
travel_insurance_interaction.notes: does standard travel insurance cover a missed connection from a cancelled ferry

public_holidays_closures._note: Covers: What Closes on a Spanish Public Holiday (and feeds the existing barcelona-august-shutdown article as a targeted addition). Dates are change-prone per year — flag accordingly.

value.name: Diada de Cataluña (National Day of Catalonia)
La Mercè (feast of Our Lady of Mercy)

barcelona_local_holidays.notes: [{name, typical_date}] — city-specific (e.g. La Mercè, Santa Eulàlia)

what_typically_closes.value: Most small shops, banks, and post offices close; large shopping malls and supermarkets in tourist areas often stay open (though with reduced hours). Many museums close, some remain open with holiday hours. Restaurants: many close, but tourist-area restaurants often remain open. Public transit runs on a 'festivo' schedule (reduced frequency).
what_typically_closes.notes: shops (small vs chain), restaurants, banks, museums, transit schedule ('horario festivo')

august_shutdown_specifics.value: In Barcelona, many non-tourist local businesses and restaurants close for at least 1–2 weeks, often around August 15 (Assumption) and the following week. Most tourist-facing establishments (Gothic Quarter, El Born, Eixample tourist strips) and malls remain open. Museums often remain open, but check individual schedules.
august_shutdown_specifics.notes: how widespread, typical closure window, what stays open (malls, tourist-facing restaurants, museums) — feeds barcelona-august-shutdown

advance_planning_note.value: RECOMMENDATION — For national/regional holidays, book restaurant reservations 3–7 days ahead; check attraction websites for holiday hours. For August, be prepared for some favorite local spots to be closed, and book ferries and hotels well in advance.
advance_planning_note.notes: RECOMMENDATION — booking restaurants/checking attraction hours around these dates
